# `scope_move_to_horizon`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the guider's move-over-horizon worker, which raises the mount until its first axle coordinate reaches zero or above (the app's "arm open"); the reply reports acceptance, not arrival.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit native handler paths) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x723f0 (64-bit guider build; no-mount return @0x72448, dispatcher handle_request @0x15dc10 appends only the id), MoveAxisFunc @0x6ba80, MoveOverHoriz @0x68e40, driver Motion @0xf04c0; 32-bit handler @0x6ce18, MoveOverHoriz @0x66614; static analysis of app 3.3.2, BaseDeviceViewModel.setArmOpen |

Registered in the guider dispatcher table; the name is not in the imager tables, so a request on 4700 reaches it through the imager's method-not-found relay (mount-and-motion R1, R2). The handler does not read params. It checks that a mount object exists and is connected; on the null or disconnected path it returns without writing a result or error, and the dispatcher adds only the id, so the client gets a reply envelope with neither result nor error (no 315). A client MUST treat such a reply as a failure (no mount). It then fails with 203 if the mount is moving and 210 if the driver cannot do motion. Otherwise it names the function detail ScopeMoveToHorizon, stores movement type 5 in the shared movement parameters and launches the movement worker; reply code 0 means the worker was launched. A launch failure forwards the thread-local error. No ViewPlan check (536) is made, and the handler changes neither equatorial mode nor the requested tracking state. The worker first commands motion, then polls the axle coordinates every 0.5 s with a 30 s deadline; a first axle coordinate of 0 or above ends it with success, after which, on that normal path, it commands a stop and waits for the mount to stop; an initial motion failure or an already-stopped status exits without that cleanup. Worker failures (320 motion or state failure, 500 axle read failure, 204 timeout) are reported asynchronously through ScopeMoveToHorizon events (which also carry close when the axle position can be read), not as reply codes. Because motion is commanded before the coordinate test, repeating the call with the arm already up can still move the mount briefly. scope_goto admits movement type 5 and stops this worker before slewing. INFERRED: the first axle coordinate is the elevation axis on alt-azimuth hardware, so a terminal complete event means the arm is open. The axle-to-sky relation in equatorial mode, stopping distance and the controller's own park handling are unresolved. The app sends this method with no params for its arm-open control; its arm-cancel control sends scope_move ["none"], which stops this worker (scope_abort_slew does not). Mount serial (firmware 9.31 and 9.75, 64-bit and 32-bit, READ): the worker sends the selected slew-rate command and north motion, then polls coordinates and movement state; its common cleanup requests an all-axis stop, but initial motion failure and an unexpected zero movement status return without it.

Side effects: Writes the shared movement type (5) and function-detail state, launches the movement worker, which sends motion and stop commands to the mount controller. Emits ScopeMoveToHorizon function events asynchronously.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_move_to_horizon"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read by the handler. The app sends no params member. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 203 | The mount reports that it is moving | `equipment is moving` |
| 210 | The mount driver does not support motion | `not supported` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

No mount or a disconnected mount gives a reply with neither result nor error (no 315); a client MUST treat it as a failure. A worker launch failure forwards the thread-local error code. Worker codes 320, 500 and 204 arrive in ScopeMoveToHorizon events, not in the reply.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"scope_move_to_horizon"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_move_to_horizon","result":0,"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, moving:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_move_to_horizon","error":"equipment is moving","code":203,"id":82}
```
